--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the parent fitness is 267.8, and population includes many forgiving strategies, maybe the archive also has some unforgiving ones."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates for 10 rounds, then defects if opponent defection rate is high and cooperates if low. The trace simulates variants that test earlier by defecting once and then cooperating, and changes the test timing and post-test mode logic.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given the parent fitness is 267.8, and the population has many forgiving strategies, I suspect the archive also has mostly forgiving strategies, and maybe no Grim Trigger. The problem statement says "improve this parent"."
STRATEGY: The parent waits 10 rounds, then defects only if the opponent has defected a lot; it never defects against always-C. The trace simulates the parent, always-C, TFT, always-D, and Grim Trigger, and revises the strategy toward early testing/exploitation with a cautious forgiving mode after punishment.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent is already a decent strategy. We can improve it by adding a test early to exploit always C"
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates for the first 10 rounds, then retaliates based on opponent defection counts and recent windows. The trace simulated the parent against always-C, slot1, and TFT-like opponents, computing scores for defecting always, cooperating always, and endgame defection. It revised the strategy into a forgiving tit-for-tat with endgame defection in the last 10 rounds.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "I think this is a solid improvement over the parent. The parent gets 300 against always C and 300 against parent. Our strategy gets 320 and 316, respectively."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, retaliates on opponent defection, forgives mostly-cooperative opponents, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates endgame defection over the last 10 rounds, then over the last 5 rounds, against always-C, parent, TFT, and slot11. It changes the endgame defection window from the last 10 rounds to the last 5 rounds and finalizes a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that defects when n >= 95.
